messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — p99 latency spike observed on streaming inference path. P95 ~ 420ms -> 1.9s, P99 ~ 1.2s -> 6.4s. Automated throttles kicked for per-customer rate windows. Paging oncall.
Alex Chen: oncall here. seeing a big bump in tail. Which dependencies look noisy? DB, auth, or config fetch?
Maya Patel: quick look — control-plane auth token store shows increased 5xxs and 429s. Metrics: token-store request rate +3x, 5xx rate spiked ~50m ago. Also a config-fetch service showing elevated latencies for feature-flag reads.
Samir Rao: logs from gateway show a flurry of retries at the proxy layer: "upstream timeout" and "429 from auth-service". Streaming stalls correspond to token refresh failures.
Diana López: customers with high-concurrency streaming (long live sessions) are seeing repeated stalls. Modalities: streaming clients holding connections open, KV cache misses on prefix lookups.
Alex Chen: can we confirm DB-side queue depth? run: `kubectl -n infra exec -c proxy db-proxy-abc -- curl -s localhost:9090/metrics | grep queue_depth`
Maya Patel: done — queue_depth ~ 480 (threshold 200). Also connection pool saturation on auth-db replicas. SQL slowdowns: `SELECT count(*) FROM tokens WHERE refreshed_at > now() - interval '1 minute'` returning slow.
Samir Rao: hypothesis: auth token-store causing backpressure -> upstream proxy queues -> streaming tail increase. Also feature-flag fetches blocking model routing causing additional head-of-line delays.
Priya Singh: adding mitigations: 1) enable auth read-replicas for token-store (read-only fallback), 2) increase proxy max-conns temporarily, 3) enable feature-flag cache TTL fallback (hard-ttl 30s). Anyone object?
Diana López: +1 to read-replica fallback. We should also throttle noisy customers rather than global rate window. Can we identify top 10 customers by concurrency?
Alex Chen: running query for top customers now. `SELECT customer_id, count(*) as sessions FROM streams WHERE state='open' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 10;` — sending results.
incident-bot: BOT NOTE: created incident ticket #INC-2026, notified status@ and posted initial status page with impacted services: streaming, inference gateway.
Maya Patel: quick patch applied to auth-proxy: fallback to read-replica for reads (PR rolled to canary). Monitoring latencies.
Samir Rao: proxy max-conns increased from 1200 -> 2000 in the gateway canary; rolling to 20% of nodes. Early signal: p95 improved 20% on canary.
Priya Singh: feature-flag cache TTL fallback deployed to control-plane; one-minute soft TTL in effect. This reduces config fetch QPS ~28% on control-plane.
Diana López: top noisy customer (cust-847) has ~35% of concurrent streams. We throttled them to limit 100 concurrent streams. Notified their account team.
Alex Chen: auth-db replica lag trending low after read fallback; queue depth falling from 480 -> 140. p99 streaming latency trending down but still elevated in some regions (eu-west).
Maya Patel: eu-west showed higher auth token store 5xxs due to regional read-replica misconfig (misrouted to primary). Fixing routing rule in service mesh.
Samir Rao: mesh rule updated. eu-west token-store 5xxs subsided. Re-run synthetic: streaming p99 now ~1.3s (from 6.4s). Still above SLO (900ms p99 target).
Priya Singh: temporary routing: canary routed heavy customers to dedicated inference pool (reserved capacity) for eu-west. This reduces contention on shared pool.
Diana López: impacting customers: 12 enterprise customers experienced degraded session experience >30s stalls. Sending heads-up for those accounts and drafting status copy.
Alex Chen: mitigation list summary in incident ticket: read-replica fallback, proxy connection increase, feature-flag TTL fallback, noisy-customer throttles, regional reroute to dedicated pool. Monitoring for 30 minutes then escalate to incident commander if not recovered.
Maya Patel: note: we also observed a surge of config fetches from internal rollout job hitting control-plane. Killed rollout job which reduced QPS by ~15%.
Samir Rao: log snippet showing retry storm:
```
2026-03-15T18:21:01Z gateway-1 ERROR upstream timeout for /v1/token refresh attempt=5 client=cust-847
2026-03-15T18:21:03Z auth-store-3 WARN read-replica conn-saturation
```
Diana López: customer-impact assessment: estimated requests affected ~ 120k streaming token requests in the 45m window. Majority recovered after mitigations. No data loss. Possible higher error rate for short-lived sessions.
Priya Singh: status update for status page draft: "We experienced elevated streaming latencies due to an auth token-store and config fetch surge causing backend queueing. Mitigations applied: read-replica fallback, proxy config changes, per-customer throttles, and routing adjustments. Service recovery in progress; we continue to monitor." Feedback?
Alex Chen: looks good. Add ETA for full recovery: 60m, and mention customers already notified.
Maya Patel: deploying followups: increase DB connection pool on token-store primary by +20 connections, backoff jitter to reduce synchronized retries.
Samir Rao: recommend postmortem owner: Maya + Samir. Action items: root-cause analysis on why rollout job spiked config fetches, improve per-customer circuit-breaker, autoscaling rules for token-store.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations completed, p99 trending to 850ms cluster-wide. Continued monitoring. Next update in 30m or on-call handoff.
Diana López: oncall handoff: I'm handing to Alex for overnight. Alex, can you pick up full incident ownership at 19:45 UTC? :raised_hand:
Alex Chen: taking handoff. I'll monitor and coordinate postmortem. Leaving notes in ticket. :thumbsup:
oncall-rotation-bot: HANDOFF LOGGED — incident #INC-2026 handed from Diana López to Alex Chen at 2026-03-15T19:45:00Z. Reminder: escalate if p99 > 900ms for >15m.
Priya Singh: adding brief remediation checklist in incident ticket and scheduling postmortem meeting tomorrow. Good job team. :party_popper:
